Answer: B
Reason: The frontal chest X-ray demonstrates a right-sided superior mediastinal widening with a slightly lobulated contour, and the lateral view confirms increased soft-tissue density in the retrotracheal space. These radiographic features are characteristic of a mediastinal lipoma, which typically presents as a well-defined, low-density (though appearing soft-tissue on plain film) mass in this location, distinguishing it from the more aggressive or cystic appearances of the other options.
